summary: The PR aims to prevent `Content-Length` from being sent alongside `Transfer-Encoding` in `res.send()`. However, by placing `!this.get('Transfer-Encoding')` on the outer `if (chunk !== undefined)` condition, the calculation of `len` is completely skipped when `Transfer-Encoding` is set. As a result, automatic ETag generation (which checks `len !== undefined`) is silently disabled for transfer-encoded responses.

findings.title: ETag header is omitted when Transfer-Encoding header is present
findings.description: In `res.send()`, adding `!this.get('Transfer-Encoding')` to the `if (chunk !== undefined)` condition causes `len` calculation and string-to-Buffer conversion to be bypassed when `Transfer-Encoding` is present. Subsequently, the check `if (generateETag && len !== undefined)` evaluates to `false` because `len` remains `undefined`. This causes Express to omit the `ETag` header for transfer-encoded responses even when ETag generation is enabled. Only setting the `Content-Length` header should be conditional on `!this.get('Transfer-Encoding')`.
findings.verificationHypothesis: When `Transfer-Encoding` is set on a response, `res.send()` should omit `Content-Length` but still generate an `ETag` header if ETag generation is enabled in the app.

suggestedReproduction.input: GET request to an endpoint that sets `Transfer-Encoding` and calls `res.send('hello world')`.
suggestedReproduction.preconditions: Default Express application settings (etag generation enabled).
suggestedReproduction.expectedBehavior: Response contains `Transfer-Encoding` and `ETag` headers, but no `Content-Length` header.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: Response contains `Transfer-Encoding`, but `ETag` header is missing.
